status_summary: Executive Order 14186, The Iron Dome for America (signed 2025-01-27, 90 FR 8767), later called Golden Dome, ordered the Defense Secretary to produce within 60 days an architecture covering defense against ballistic, hypersonic and advanced cruise missiles from peer, near-peer and rogue adversaries, accelerated space tracking sensors, proliferated space-based interceptors for boost-phase intercept and underlayer and terminal defenses. Executive Order 14369 (signed 2025-12-18) later set a 2028 date for demonstrating next-generation missile defense prototypes and required a report on air and missile defense industrial gaps within 90 days. Congress provided about 25 billion dollars in the July 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21, whose Sec. 20003 is titled Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for integrated air and missile defense) (about 90 percent obligated by mid-August 2026), the Pentagon's cost estimate is 185 billion dollars, and in July 2026 the Space Development Agency awarded 1.75 billion dollars for 36 tracking satellites. The older programs the Mandate names have lagged: in June 2025 Defense News reported the Next Generation Interceptor (NGI) about 18 months behind schedule and the Glide Phase Interceptor about three years behind, with no purchase quantity for NGI given; no quantity of 64 was found. The FY2027 request is 17.9 billion dollars per Aerospace America (about 17.1 billion through a planned reconciliation bill), and Air & Space Forces Magazine reported in October 2026 that Golden Dome has no FY2026 appropriation, so it has no baseline under the continuing resolution that began 2026-10-01; the program director warned in August 2026 that without FY2027 funding there would be no Golden Dome. Homeland cruise missile defense funding and the Mandate's call to keep homeland missile defense out of arms control talks were not verified.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14186, The Iron Dome for America (signed 2025-01-27, published 2025-02-03 at 90 FR 8767), orders a reference architecture and implementation plan within 60 days covering defense against ballistic, hypersonic and advanced cruise missiles from peer, near-peer and rogue adversaries, accelerated space tracking sensors, proliferated space-based interceptors for boost-phase intercept, and underlayer and terminal defenses.

Defense News reports the Missile Defense Agency's FY2026 request of 10.2 billion dollars; NGI is about 18 months behind with no buy quantity given, the Glide Phase Interceptor about three years behind, and 25 billion dollars was requested for Golden Dome within a supplemental spending bill under debate.

The reconciliation law P.L. 119-21 is enacted; its Sec. 20003 is titled Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for integrated air and missile defense. An October 2026 Air & Space Forces Magazine report says it provides about 25 billion dollars for Golden Dome, about 90 percent obligated by mid-August 2026.
timeline.source: GovInfo (Public Law 119-21); Air & Space Forces Magazine

timeline.event: Executive Order 14369, Ensuring American Space Superiority (published 2025-12-23 at 90 FR 60537), calls for next-generation missile defense prototypes to be developed and demonstrated by 2028, tied to Executive Order 14186, and a report within 90 days on technology, supply chain and industrial gaps for air and missile defense. The text does not mention Golden Dome, space-based interceptors or directed energy by name.

Budget briefing materials show a 17.9 billion dollar FY2027 Golden Dome request, about 17.1 billion of it through a planned reconciliation package; officials acknowledged Congress may not approve that funding.
Space Development Agency awards 1.75 billion dollars to L3Harris and Sierra Space for 36 missile-tracking satellites in Tranche 3, with launches possible in late 2028.

Program director Gen. Guetlein warns of a funding shortfall for FY2027. He cites a June 2026 test at White Sands, groundbreaking at the first operational site in Virginia, and a Space Force prize competition for space-based interceptors aiming at initial capability by 2028.

Senators of both parties urge a bipartisan funding path after a 2026-09-29 hearing; the report says Golden Dome has no FY2026 appropriation, the cost estimate is 185 billion dollars, and the FY2027 request is 17 billion via reconciliation plus 400 million in the base budget.

Reports differ on FY2027 request details: Aerospace America (April 2026) says 17.9 billion dollars with about 17.1 billion through reconciliation, while Air & Space Forces Magazine (October 2026) says 17 billion through reconciliation plus 400 million base. A reference article had said Congress passed 13.4 billion dollars for Golden Dome in February 2026, but the October 2026 report says there is no FY2026 appropriation; The October report was followed and the reference-article dates (2025-05-20, 2025-07-21, 2025-09-01, 2026-03-01) were dropped. Executive Order 14186 was re-read in the Federal Register (90 FR 8767) and Executive Order 14369 (90 FR 60537) was added; P.L. 119-21 was checked only through its table of contents (Sec. 20003), so the 25 billion dollar figure rests on Air & Space Forces Magazine and the Defense News report of the pending bill.
